question: What is the main job of the true pelvis during childbirth?

options.A: Acting as the bony birth canal for the baby
options.B: Supporting the entire weight of the upper spine
options.C: Anchoring the major muscles of the lower thighs
options.D: Protecting the kidneys and upper abdominal organs

explanation: The true pelvis sits below the pelvic brim and forms the rigid channel that the fetus navigates during labor. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is the bony pelvis shaped like a basin?

options.A: To allow the developing fetus to float freely in the abdominal cavity
options.B: To increase the total volume of fluid inside the pregnant uterus
options.C: To prevent any movement whatsoever in the lower half of the body
options.D: To effectively transfer upper body weight and protect reproductive organs

explanation: Its ring-like, basin shape provides structural strength while housing and shielding delicate internal pelvic structures. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which three bones join together to form each hip bone?
explanation: During childhood and growth, the ilium, ischium, and pubis fuse at the acetabulum to create a single hip bone on each side. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the name of the small, tail-like bone at the bottom of the sacrum?
explanation: The coccyx is the terminal segment of the spinal column and provides a slight amount of movement during fetal descent. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h2)

question: What causes the pelvic joints to become loose and movable during pregnancy?

options.A: Rapid stretching of the overlying skin
options.B: Increased calcium deposits in the cartilage
options.C: The release of pregnancy hormones like relaxin
options.D: Direct pressure from the heavy fetal head

explanation: Hormones produced during gestation specifically target pelvic ligaments and joints to prepare the pelvis for childbirth. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h3)

question: Where is the pubic symphysis located in the pelvis?

options.A: At the very bottom tip of the tailbone
options.B: On the upper wing of the iliac crest
options.C: At the front, joining the two pubic bones
options.D: At the back, connecting the spine to the hip

explanation: The pubic symphysis sits right at the front middle, uniting the left and right pubic bones. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which ligament runs from the sacrum to the ischial spine?
explanation: The sacrospinous ligament spans horizontally from the lateral border of the sacrum and coccyx to the prominent ischial spine. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main role of the pelvic ligaments during pregnancy and labor?

options.A: To produce the hormones that soften the cervix before delivery
options.B: To actively push the baby down through the birth canal during contractions
options.C: To limit excessive movement of the pelvic bones while allowing necessary stretch
options.D: To completely lock the joints so no movement can occur

explanation: Ligaments provide structural stability, preventing the pelvis from over-separating while still permitting slight give during birth. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h4)

question: What anatomical landmark marks the boundary between the false and true pelvis?
explanation: The pelvic brim acts as the dividing line separating the upper false pelvis from the lower true pelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following describes the false pelvis?

options.A: It lies above the pelvic brim and supports the pregnant uterus
options.B: It forms the rigid, narrow bony canal for fetal descent
options.C: It is bounded below by the pelvic outlet and perineum
options.D: It contains the ischial spines used to measure engagement

explanation: The false pelvis is part of the abdominal cavity framework, holding abdominal contents and the expanding uterus. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h5)

question: During a vaginal examination in labor, a midwife feels the ischial spines. What are these landmarks used to assess?

options.A: Checking the degree of cervical effacement
options.B: Estimating the total amniotic fluid volume
options.C: Determining the station of the presenting fetal part
options.D: Measuring the exact blood pressure of the mother

explanation: The ischial spines represent zero station, serving as the crucial reference point for how far the baby has descended into the pelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized pelvic shape in obstetrics?
explanation: The four classic pelvic shapes are gynecoid, android, anthropoid, and platypelloid; pyramidal is not one of them. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h6)
